newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses mixed despite Wall St record run.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses mixed despite Wall St record run.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Tuesday with London climbing sharply on the strength of Wall Street's fourth consecutive record close but others were in the doldrums.
On currency markets, the dollar weakened against the mark in early European trade but gained on the yen because of weaker-than-expected data on Japan's economic performance in September.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, made the strongest showing registering a 0.5 percent gain in early deals. Investors clearly were encouraged by Wall Street but fears over rising interest rates persisted.
"Wall Street continues to defy gravity and in London we're not far away from levels at which people will start to get interested," said one senior sales trader.

The Dow Jones industrial average finished at 6,255.60 on Monday, eclipsing Friday's record close of 6,219.82. The drive into record territory came as investors bet that interest rates will fall, making stocks even more attractive.
The Dow's bull run is the biggest boom since a seven-session record streak in February. Last week's 198-point post-election rally was the second-biggest weekly point gain ever.
The gains have been fuelled by the prospect that the U.S. Federal Reserve central bank will hold monetary policy steady at this Wednesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.

But in London, worries of rising British interest rates could continue to hold the market in check, some traders said. Others judged such fears to be overdone and were optimistic over prospects for the market.
Still, domestic economic trends took on added significance in recent weeks after rates were raised a quarter point at the end of October to douse possible inflation pressures.

Bank of England Governor Eddie George repeated on Monday his warning that interest rates would probably need to rise again if the government was to meet its 2.5 percent inflation target. Fears of higher rates continued to bear down on shares.

In Frankfurt, floor trading slipped in and out of the minus column with investors held back by a weaker dollar but drawing some comfort from Wall Street. Computerised transactions were showing a small loss in early trade.
French stocks posted modest gains at the opening but slipped back by 0.3 percent later, though traders said the underlying trend was positive, buoyed by Wall Street's strength.
The dollar, though weaker against the mark, gained momentum against the yen amid weaker-than-expected Japanese machinery orders for September, which fell 10.2 percent from August.

"It (the machinery orders figure) is weaker than expected. The market was looking for a negative number but not that negative...The bottom line is that the economy is not behaving in a manner that is threatening to inflation at the moment," said Ian Gunner, international economist at Chase Investment bank.
Dollar was at 1.4935 against the mark, half a pfennig down on the levels in late European trading on Monday.
"It's (dollar/mark) a little bit soggy...But better supported at these levels," said Brian Hilliard, senior international economist at Societe Generale Straus Turnbull.

Underlying mark strength has also been attributed by some to jitters over the EMU stability pact after Juergen Stark, German state secretary for the finance ministry, said there was no consensus about it.
CURRENCIES AT 1020 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4935 marks and 111.40 yen, compared with 1.4983 marks and 111.20 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1020 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 15.0 points higher at 3,929.4.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 1.41 points at 2,729.73.
PARIS - The CAC 40 index was down 6.72 points at 2198.48
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1020 GMT
Gold was quoted at $381.90 an ounce, compared to $380.75 at the close on Monday. Silver was higher at $4.89, up two cents.
